2015_086_111715mtg.paragraph: The Troy School District Board of Education met in regular session on Monday, November 17, 2015 at 7:00 p.m. in the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan. The packet pairs a consent agenda -- board workshop and October 20, 2015 meeting minutes, the September 2015 Treasurer's Report showing total disbursements of $10,249,141.68, and a teacher resignation -- with personnel, bid award, policy and bond items. The largest single action is Bid 9813, mechanical, electrical and plumbing upgrades at Athens and Troy High Schools, recommended for award at $8,777,899.90 against a combined budget of 9,833,131.00. Assistant Superintendent Rick West also reported that the district's operating millage renewal passed on November 3, 2015.

## Meeting
Regular meeting of the Troy School District Board of Education, Monday, November 17, 2015, 7:00 p.m., Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098; district offices at 4400 Livernois, 248.823.4000. Broadcast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW); video at vimeo.com/troyschools.

## Recognition and consent agenda
Mission Moment: the Larson Middle School 8th grade Stream Leaders program, advisor Sandra Bammel, sponsored by the Clinton River Watershed Council. Consent items: board workshop minutes (agenda lists October 1, 2015; the attached minutes are headed October 6, 2015), October 20, 2015 meeting minutes, the September 2015 Treasurer's Report, and a teacher resignation. The October 20 minutes record resolutions 15-092 through 15-097, each carried 7 Yes / 0 No, including recognition of sixty-eight National Merit Scholarship semifinalists and acceptance of the Yeo & Yeo audit of the 2014-2015 fiscal year presented by audit partner David Youngstrom.

## Personnel and business
Item 6.A: a 2015-2016 probationary contract for Jennifer A. Locke, 1.0 first grade teacher at Martell Elementary. Item 6.B appoints negotiating teams for TEA, TESA and TESPA contracts expiring June 30, 2016, with Jordan Harris as chief spokesperson. Item 8.A reports that operating millages set to expire at the end of 2015 were renewed by voters on November 3, 2015. Item 8.B adopts the annual summer tax resolution to levy one-half of school property taxes including debt service beginning with 2016. Item 8.C awards Bid 9814 musical instruments at $124,357.00 (Washington Music Center $92,010.00; Sam Ash Corporation $747.00; Brook Mays Music $31,600.00). Item 8.D awards Bid 9813 MEP upgrades: Athens High School $5,986,790.00 and Troy High School $2,791,110.49, total awards $8,777,899.90 against a budget of 9,833,131.00, a stated bid savings of $1,055,231.10.

## Other
First readings of Board Policy E-1102, Use of School Buildings and Facilities, and new Board Policy D-1401, Reimbursement of Board Member or Employee Expenses (MCL 380.1254), both to be voted in December. Under Policy B-2001, Vice President Mr. Schmidt is approved to attend the 2015 NAIS People of Color Conference, Tampa, Florida, December 3-5, 2015. Rick West closes with a 2013 Bond Program Series 1 construction update by Barton Malow and TMP.

Troy School District (Oakland County, Michigan) Board of Education regular meeting packet for Monday, November 17, 2015, 7:00 p.m., Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098. District administration is at 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098, 248.823.4000, www.troy.k12.mi.us; meetings are carried on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) Mondays and Wednesdays at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m., with video at vimeo.com/troyschools.

**Recognition and consent agenda.** The TSD Mission Moment featured Larson Middle School 8th grade science teacher Sandra Bammel and the Stream Leaders program, sponsored by the Clinton River Watershed Council, begun at Larson in fall 2013; presenters were Sabrina Badia, Rosemary Northcote, Audrey Parks and Alexa Withun. Consent items A-D: board workshop minutes (agenda item 5.A cites October 1, 2015 while the attached minutes are headed October 6, 2015), minutes of the October 20, 2015 meeting, the September 2015 Treasurer's Report, and a teacher resignation.

**Workshop minutes, October 6, 2015, Administration Building.** Called to order by President Philippart at 6:00 p.m. with Mrs. Edmunds, Mr. Hauff, Mr. Schmidt and Ms. Underwood; absent Mrs. Fleming and Mr. Miletti. Also present: Superintendent Machesky, administrators West, Maynard, Dziatczak, Griffor and Harris, and Yeo & Yeo auditors. Agenda: the Yeo & Yeo audit report, the S.O.C. Hold Harmless Millage, bond expenditure for the Troy High/Athens MEP work, employee evaluation, professional development for 2015/2016, a millage update, and input on proposed MASB amendments. Adjourned 8:50 p.m.; submitted by Paula Fleming, Secretary.

**Meeting minutes, October 20, 2015, Services Building.** All seven members present, along with four high school student representatives, administrators Machesky, Dziatczak, Griffor, Harris, Gottlieb, Roncone, Silagy and West, and approximately 25 audience members. Dr. Machesky noted that more than one million students from some 22,000 high schools entered the National Merit Scholarship Program and only 16,000 seniors are named semifinalists; Troy has sixty-eight, recognized at an October 14th reception at Athens High School. That resolution, moved by Ms. Underwood and supported by Mr. Miletti, passed 7-0 and was signed the twentieth day of October, 2015. A Mission Moment recognized Troy High senior Nithya Ramadurai of the Build On chapter. Resolution 15-092 (Hauff/Schmidt, 7-0) approved September 1, September 15 special and closed session, and September 15 meeting minutes plus the August 2015 Treasurer's Report. Resolution 15-093 (Fleming/Edmunds, 7-0) approved new hires Sara Cavataio and Andrea Polite. Jordan Harris, Assistant Superintendent for Employee Services, reported on the fourth year of the Troy Educator Appraisal Model (TEAM) and state performance ratings of highly effective, effective, minimally effective and ineffective. Resolution 15-094 (Miletti/Underwood, 7-0) seated the 2015-2016 Sex Education Advisory Board with co-chairs Amy Buchanan and Nicole Jenkins. Mark Dziatczak and Kris Griffor reported on 2015-2016 professional development and on post-secondary attainment, including dual enrollment at Oakland Community College for Niles and IB Diploma coursework at the International Academy. Resolution 15-095 (Hauff/Miletti, 7-0) accepted the audited 2015 financial statements presented by David Youngstrom, Audit Partner, Yeo & Yeo, whose future-challenges list covered fringe benefit cost, state economic and political conditions, retirement rate increases, uncertainty of state revenue, special education costs, unfunded pension liability and new accounting standards. Resolution 15-097 (Fleming/Hauff, 7-0) adopted board committee assignments. Dr. Machesky reported attending the Deep Learning Lab Conference in Seattle at the invitation of Oakland Schools Superintendent Wanda Cook-Robinson, with Oakland Schools covering the cost. Adjourned 9:40 p.m.

**Personnel.** Item 6.A recommends a probationary contract for the 2015-2016 school year for Jennifer A. Locke, 1.0 first grade teacher at Martell Elementary; M.A., Marygrove College, 2011 and B.S., Central Michigan University, 2005; prior positions at Kingsbury Country Day School (January 2015-October 2015), Huron Academy (August 2013-December 2014), Schroeder Elementary (April 2013-June 2013) and Michigan Technical Academy (August 2006-June 2012); resident of Lake Orion. Item 6.B appoints negotiating teams for TEA/MEA/NEA (teaching staff), TESA/MEA/NEA (secretarial) and TESPA/MEA/NEA (para-educators and skilled trades), all contracts expiring June 30, 2016, with Jordan Harris as chief spokesperson and members Rick West, Mark Dziatczak, Kris Griffor and Dave Pass, plus Stephanie Maynard and Carmen White on the TESA and TESPA teams.

**Business.** Item 8.A: operating millages were set to expire at the end of 2015 and the renewal passed on November 3, 2015; Rick West presented the results. Item 8.B adopts the annual summer tax resolution under 1976 P.A. 451, as amended, to collect one-half of school property taxes including debt service beginning with 2016 and continuing for the 2016-2017 fiscal year, to be forwarded to the City of Troy and received before January 1, 2016, with collection expenses negotiable under MCLA 380.1612 and notice under the Open Meetings Act (Act 267, P.A. 1976). Item 8.C awards Bid 9814, Musical Instruments and Supplies for Athens and Troy High Schools (memo from Purchasing Supervisor Todd Hensley, 1440 Rankin, Troy, Michigan 48093, November 4, 2015; reviewed by Fine Arts Coordinator Carrie Peyok and band directors Brian Nutting and Jeff McCoy): Washington Music Center $92,010.00, Sam Ash Corporation $747.00, Brook Mays Music $31,600.00, total $124,357.00 from the Capital Projects Fund; bid tabulation grand totals were Brook Mays $90,214.00, Marshall Music $146,814.00, Sam Ash $75,146.00 and Washington $128,805.00. Item 8.D awards Bid 9813, issued September 22, 2015, for MEP upgrades, proposals received October 29, 2015 and reviewed by Director of Maintenance and Operations Rob Carson with TMP Associates, Peter Basso & Associates and Barton Malow: Athens High School general trades Titan Ind. $377,489.00, mechanical Ecker Mechanical $4,301,000.00, electrical Metro Electric $1,308,300.00, total $5,986,790.00; Troy High School general trades Titan Ind. $239,610.49, mechanical Contrast Mechanical $2,240,000.00, electrical J & J Electric $311,500.00, total $2,791,110.49. The Barton Malow letter of November 4, 2015 from project manager Christa Amalio (26500 American Drive, Southfield, Michigan 48034) states TOTAL AWARDS $8,777,899.90 against a combined budget of 9,833,131.00 and a bid savings of $1,055,231.10, notes no bids received for roofing, and shows Titan's Athens value as $377,489.51.

**Other.** First reading of revisions to Board Policy E-1102, Use of School Buildings and Facilities (adopted February 16, 1976; revised January 16, 1979, September 19, 1989, April 21, 1998 and November 17, 2015; cross-referencing Policy K-1501). First reading of new Board Policy D-1401, Reimbursement of Board Member or Employee Expenses, with nine pre-approved categories, mileage at the Internal Revenue Service rate, no reimbursement of spouse expenses, and legal reference MCL 380.1254; both go to the December consent agenda. Under Policy B-2001, the Board approves Vice President Mr. Schmidt's attendance at the 28th NAIS People of Color Conference, Tampa, Florida, December 3-5, 2015. Item 10.D is Rick West's bond projects update, attaching a Barton Malow / TMP construction update on BP#5 Troy High School Area J classroom addition, BP#6 Boulan Park and Larson office additions, BP#8 Athens High School mechanical and electrical upgrades bid and awarded November 17, 2015, and 2016 work: BP#16 International Academy and Hamilton Elementary, partial roof replacement at six schools, and site improvements and paving at Barnard, Schroeder, Smith MS, Athens and Troy High School, all bidding in January.
